subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial

Subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial

Hi Jordan / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation and really excited about the potential fit between ACME and Redwood. As discussed, I wanted to capture a concise POC plan and the environment options so your security and infra teams can weigh in. I attached the draft POC plan and a short network requirements spreadsheet.

Summary of goals / success criteria
- 2-week functional evaluation that validates: latency < 200ms p50 on your sample query set, response quality parity with your current baseline on 5 key prompts, and stable throughput of ~10 q/s sustained.
- Minimal data leakage: logs retained per your policy, no customer data persisted beyond the trial unless you opt in.
- Clear handoff path for production readiness (if POC passed).

Environment options (pros/cons):
1) Hosted Redwood trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted environment, no infra changes on your side. Pros: quickest to stand up (~48 hours), easy instrumentation and metrics. Cons: requires using our hosted endpoints and agreeing to our standard trial data handling.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity in our hosted infra): Pros: closer to production performance, predictable throughput. Cons: ~1-week provisioning lead time and commit for reserved capacity during POC window.
3) VPC trial (VPC peering / private deployment): Pros: meets strict security requirements (data stays in your VPC), logs under your control. Cons: longer setup (1-2 weeks), network changes and firewall rules required, requires infra owner engagement.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0: finalize environment choice and kickoff call (schedule below).
- Week 1-2: run test plans, ingest sample prompts, measure latency/quality/throughput.
- End of Week 2: POC review and go/no-go.

Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa (commercial/coordination), Nikhil (SE lead / technical setup).
- ACME: Jordan (product owner), Samir (infra/security).

Next steps / asks for you
- Which environment do you prefer to start with (hosted or VPC)? If VPC, please share your infra contact and preferred time for a network kickoff.
- Confirm sample dataset and the 5 priority prompts (attach if available).
- Availability for a 30-min kickoff next week — proposed slots: Tue 6/30 10-11am PT or Wed 7/1 1-2pm PT.

Attachments: acmeai_poc_plan_v1.pdf, network_requirements.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to getting this underway.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / Vivek —

Thanks for the note. Quick technical read on the options and recommended approach for ACME's stated success criteria:

Recommendation: start with a 48-72 hour hosted smoke test to validate quality and basic latency, then pivot to a VPC trial for the 2-week throughput and security evaluation. That minimizes time-to-insight and keeps security happy.

Hosted smoke test (what we need / steps)
- Redwood creates a short-lived API key & sandbox project scoped to ACME (no persistent data by default).
- Provide sample prompts + test harness (we can host a simple script that your PM runs).
- We enable verbose latency and token-level metrics.
- Estimated ops time: 4-6 hours to provision and validate.

VPC trial (what we need / steps)
- VPC peering or PrivateLink setup (we prefer PrivateLink where available).
- CIDR/IP ranges: we will provide our public endpoint IPs in the network_requirements.xlsx; your infra needs to whitelist those and allow TLS outbound/inbound per the sheet.
- SSH not required; we use mTLS/TLS endpoints.
- Estimated ops time: 1-2 business days with your network team engaged.

Compute sizing suggestion for trial (to hit ~10 q/s)
- Start with 4 concurrent vGPU instances (T4-equivalent) under continuous batching. We can scale down/up after baseline measurement to optimize costs.

Potential gotchas
- If ACME wants token-level logging disabled, we need to capture that in the POC plan (affects debugging and metrics).
- For very low-latency tail requirements, we should validate prompt lengths used in your sample set.

I'll prep a short checklist and a provisioning request we can hand to ACME's infra team. Should I send that to Jordan & Samir directly, or would you prefer to be the initial point of contact?

- Nikhil

3) Owners:

5) Docs & attachments: acmeai_poc_plan_v1.pdf (POC success criteria + evaluation plan), network_requirements.xlsx (IP ranges and firewall checklist).

If Jordan prefers we start directly in VPC, we can shift - Nikhil estimates a 1-2 day setup once your infra engages. For speed and to ensure we can show quality quickly, we recommend starting hosted and then flip to VPC for security validation.
